topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic establishes the opening administrative framing and outlines the core learning outcomes for the lecture.

topics.label: Intrinsic and Environmental Determinants of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the fundamental origins of cancer by evaluating the interplay between intrinsic genetic mutations, stochastic cellular events, and environmental factors supported by epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Carcinogenic Initiation and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular and cellular processes through which exposures drive malignancy via direct DNA damage, xenobiotic metabolic activation, chronic inflammation, and promotional signaling.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify mutational signatures and verify the carcinogenicity of specific agents.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing summary of the lecture, reflecting on the everyday risk-benefit assessments associated with carcinogen exposures.
